text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for route /v1/generate (redwood-13b-qt) — sustained p99 > 1200ms for 3m, p95 ~ 480ms. Streaming stalls observed on ~12% of requests. Paging oncall@infra. :rotating_light:

oncall: acknowledged. pinging infra. collecting logs now.

sasha: seeing a bunch of 'CUDA ECC corrected' messages and thermal warnings on gpu-node-03. logs: `gpu-node-03 kernel: GPU0: ce corrected 23 events` — could be noisy ECC. p99 aligns with when node started returning corrected ECCs.

priya: is this affecting dedicated pools or hosted? telemetry shows spike concentrated on pool 'gpu.p-fleet-8' which contains gpu-node-03 and gpu-node-07. Multi-node pattern.

jason: streaming agent traces show stalls at KV cache lookups timed out around the same window. suspect long tail due to hardware retries causing driver stalls. p99 timelines match ECC surge.

maya: customer impact: several prod apps reported increased latency and 429s from client-side timeouts. CS triage: 3 paying customers > 2% error rate. Need immediate mitigation and customer comms.

infra-bot: RUNBOOK: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/gpu-ecc-thermal — recommended immediate actions: 1) divert traffic away from affected nodes, 2) reduce concurrency to the pool, 3) initiate node quarantine and healthcheck.

sasha: taking node out of rotation now — kubectl drain gpu-node-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data. Starting cordon.

priya: I can update routing policy to avoid pool 'gpu.p-fleet-8' for new requests. Applying policy patch to route by latency tier to fallback pool 'gpu.p-fleet-2' (lower latency SLO but adequate).

jason: patch applied. Traffic is shifting — backend metrics show 60% of new requests routed to fallback, p99 trending down but streaming tail still at ~700ms for older in-flight requests.

oncall: are we running any heavy background compactions or maintenance on those nodes?

sasha: not that I can see. Kernel shows thermal trip counts incrementing and GPU fan speed oscillating. I suspect a flaky thermal sensor causing repeated recovery cycles.

maya: CS: preparing a short note to impacted customers: "We're investigating intermittent latency; we have rerouted traffic and are actively remediating GPU host issues. We'll update in 30m." Approving — please add ETA if known.

infra-bot: checklist update: mark node quarantined, run `nvmlDeviceGetTemperature` health probes, collect dmesg and nvidia-smi -q.

sasha: dmesg attached snippet: ```GPU0: smc thermal watcher: temp_normal->temp_high
GPU0: ECC corrected errors: 47
radeon: thermal trip detected
``` and nvidia-smi shows ECC corrected counts increasing. Uploading to incident artifacts.

priya: I increased KV cache retention for streaming sessions by +20% to reduce lookup ops from hitting the GPU for recent prefixes. That should help ongoing in-flight tails.

jason: confirmed: KV hit rate increased and streaming stalls reduced for rerouted requests. p95 back to 200ms, p99 ~ 300ms after mitigation on fallback pool.

sasha: node gpu-node-03 is in maintenance; running `ipmitool sensor` shows CPU temp fine but GPUs report thermal events. I'm going to force a GPU reset via driver tools and if that doesn't stabilize, we'll isolate and replace.

infra-bot: NOTE: GPU reset may drop existing sessions — expect transient errors. Use careful pacing.

oncall: can we avoid user-visible errors? any graceful fallback?

priya: yes, we have fallback models on CPU-paths and smaller quantized variants. For persistent errors we'll add an automatic fallback for affected requests (policy: retry->route alternate model). Implementing a temporary retry policy: 2 fast retries to alternate pool.

maya: CS: sending updated note: "We've routed traffic to alternative capacity and initiated GPU host remediation. We're monitoring. Next update in 30m or on stable recovery."

jason: after reset, GPUs still reporting intermittent ECC corrections. Node remains quarantined. Planning hot-swap with gpu-node-14 from spare pool.

sasha: coordinating physical replacement with data center tech. ETA 90 minutes for swap.

infra-bot: escalation: hardware team paged. Please add post-incident action: run long-term ECC stress test on replaced GPU, update model routing to prefer pools with lower ECC history.

priya: I've flagged all customers affected and offered reduced rate credit proactively. Logged customer tickets for follow-up.

oncall: postmortem note — initial cause hypothesis: flaky GPU thermal sensor causing repeated recoveries and ECC correction events leading to driver-level stalls and long tail latency. Mitigations: traffic diversion, KV cache tuning, retry fallback to alternate pools, node quarantine and hardware swap.

maya: agreeing — I'll coordinate external comms after postmortem draft.

jason: monitoring shows p99 now stabilized near pre-incident after diversion. Continuing to watch for 1h.

sasha: adding final logs and command history to artifacts: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-03; kubectl drain gpu-node-03 --force` and ipmi logs.

infra-bot: INCIDENT BOT: incident severity reduced to Sev3. If metrics re-escalate to p99>1000ms reopen.

oncall: closing initial paging loop. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

maya: action items assigned: sasha (hardware swap + artifacts), jason (monitoring dashboards + verify fallbacks), priya (routing policy change + customer tickets), maya (external comms). We'll sync in 60m for postmortem sketch.

incident-bot: Incident archived to /incidents/1730002468 — runbook link and artifacts attached.
